subject: Retention exception request & log deletion details (Helios Bank)
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@heliosbank.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Helios Security Team <security@heliosbank.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Request: retention exception & deletion confirmation for Helios PII logs

Hannah —

Thanks for taking this. We are working through the SIG and CAIQ for our new vendor onboarding and have one item that needs clarity before we close: Helios requires a documented exception if any application-level request/response logs containing high-sensitivity PII are retained beyond 90 days.

Current ask: can Redwood confirm whether any request/response logs containing customer PII or tokens are stored outside of ephemeral KV cache for >90 days (by default)? If yes, we need a formal exception process and a sample filled exception form for internal approvers. If no, please confirm the deletion policy and how deletions are audited (e.g., deletion job timestamps, S3 lifecycle, audit log record ids).

Also, any diagram or short note on how you separate telco/ingest logs from the model KV cache would help our reviewers.

Can you route to security or legal if needed and send the exception form if applicable. We are aiming to sign the agreement by EOW this week.

—Samir
Samir Patel
VP, Vendor Risk Management
Helios Bank

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@heliosbank.com>
Cc: Helios Security Team <security@heliosbank.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Feb 2026 10:07:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: retention exception & deletion confirmation for Helios PII logs

Samir —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front:
- Default: Redwood does NOT persist model request/response payloads containing user content or model tokens beyond short-term serving caches. By default we keep request/response logs for 30 days for operational debugging.
- Exceptions: We support customer-requested retention exceptions (e.g., for compliance or legal hold) through a formal retention-exception workflow that includes an approval chain and scoped S3 buckets.
- Auditability: Deletions are recorded as audit events (deletion_job_id, timestamp, operator_id) and the underlying objects are removed from S3 and marked in our audit index. I will attach a one-page SOC 2 summary and a filled sample exception form.

I copied Marcus to confirm the operational details and Neha for procurement cadence. Marcus — can you confirm whether the 30-day default applies to both hosted and dedicated deployments and whether we can support a 180-day scoped exception for Helios in Hosted with encryption-at-rest and customer KMS?

I'll follow up with the form pre-filled for Helios and the log retention table.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@heliosbank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Feb 2026 14:32:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: retention exception & deletion confirmation for Helios PII logs

Samir / team —

Confirming what Hannah wrote and adding operational nuance:
- Hosted (API): default 30-day request/response retention for logs that are persisted for debugging/observability. Logs stored in encrypted S3 buckets; lifecycle rules purge objects after 30 days by default.
- Dedicated: for Dedicated customers we can configure retention per contract; default builds often mirror Hosted but retention is configurable at workspace level.
- Exception process: we require an exception form (attached), justification, and security review. For exceptions >90 days we require customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-KMS) or an approved encryption key policy, and we schedule quarterly access reviews.
- Deletion verification: we provide a deletion manifest (CSV) with object ids and deletion_job_id; manifests are retained in our audit store for 7 years (indexes only, not the content).

Attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (control mappings), retention-exception-form-Helios.xlsx (pre-filled), log-retention-table.csv (sample manifest format).

Samir — if Helios wants 180 days for select troubleshooting logs, we can scope it to a named workspace and set a retention TTL and customer KMS key. Can you confirm the exact categories Helios must keep (request/response bodies, stack traces, or only metadata)?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure Security
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Helios Security Team <security@heliosbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@heliosbank.com>, Ava Chong <ava.chong@heliosbank.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: retention exception & deletion confirmation for Helios PII logs

Marcus / Hannah —

Thanks for the detail and attachments. A few clarifying questions before we move to legal sign-off:
1) For the hosted option with a 180-day exception, can you confirm whether full request/response bodies (which may include PII) will be stored in an S3 bucket accessible only by Redwood ops via a role, or whether they are persisted in a separate internal datastore?
2) We need the deletion manifest to include a cryptographic hash (SHA256) per object and the S3 object key so we can verify deletion. Can Redwood provide that?
3) Does Redwood preserve any derived telemetry (e.g., embeddings, reranking scores) that could be used to reconstruct PII after deletion? If so, what controls are in place?
4) For auditing, can you provide sample audit_event_ids for a deletion job and a short excerpt of the audit event format (redacted) so our team knows what to expect?

If you can answer these and confirm the exception workflow timeline (typical approvals take 5 business days) we can proceed.

—Helios Security

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Helios Security Team <security@heliosbank.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@heliosbank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Feb 2026 17:40:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: retention exception & deletion confirmation for Helios PII logs

Team —

Answers below, and attached the requested redacted examples. High level: we can satisfy your 180-day scoped exception in Hosted with the controls you requested. Details: 

1) Storage location: for hosted 180-day exceptions we place the scoped objects in a customer-named, dedicated S3 prefix within an encrypted bucket. Access is limited to a scoped ops role and to the customer if using BYOK (customer KMS). We do NOT store those objects in a separate internal datastore.

2) Deletion manifest: yes — we can provide a manifest with S3 object key, SHA256 hash, deletion_job_id, and timestamp. The manifest itself is signed (internal HMAC) and delivered via a secure Drive link. See attached log-retention-table.csv (sample).

3) Derived telemetry: we do not persist embeddings or other derived artifacts that could reconstruct PII beyond the same retention window unless explicitly requested in the exception. By default embeddings are ephemeral for caching and are rotated; any longer-term derived store is subject to the same exception controls.

4) Audit events: sample (redacted) event: "deletion_job_id=del-20260204-77f, operator=ops-service, timestamp=2026-02-04T16:22:11Z, deleted_keys=[s3://redwood-logs/helios/ws-123/req-4321.json], manifest_id=man-20260204-09". We can provide a paginated audit export if needed for your audit team.

Next steps:
- Please confirm the categories Helios will require for the 180-day window (we suggest: request/response bodies filtered to only transactions tagged by Helios workspace id; exclude system debug dumps).
- If confirmed, we'll generate a final exception document and DocuSign package (link will be shared).

We appended the pre-filled exception form and the SOC2 summary PDF in the Drive link for your records.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Security PM | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf; retention-exception-form-Helios.xlsx; log-retention-table.csv
